page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine instance within the High Clock Speed instance family. Driven by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8269CY processor, it supplies 40 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 20 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration integrates 192 GB of system memory, providing 4.8 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside a 35 MB shared L3 cache and support for AVX-512 with VNNI extensions. The server does not include local disk storage or hardware GPUs, relying on network-attached block storage and offering a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark measurements position the ecs.hfg6.10xlarge in the average performance tier across general computational and memory metrics. Under synthetic testing, the instance logged a PassMark CPU score of 34,691.95 and a multi-core stress-ng rating of 38,378.07. Geekbench testing yielded scores of 1,289 for single-core execution and 12,045 for multi-core throughput. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth reached 108.89 GB/sec read and 48.09 GB/sec write. In simulated real-world scenarios, the system sustained 34.78 million Redis SET operations per second and delivered 25.35 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance balances high clock frequency against a 1:4.8 vCPU-to-memory allocation. The absence of local solid-state storage necessitates remote storage provisioning, which introduces dependency on network-based I/O latency. Workload fit is targeted at enterprise applications benefiting from sustained clock speeds, such as relational database servers, enterprise web backends, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and mid-tier in-memory data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is a high clock speed virtual server configured with 40 dedicated vCPUs and 192 GB of RAM on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 3.1 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it features hardware vector instructions including AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring attached network disks, and is equipped with a 12 Gbps baseline network interface. It also lacks hardware GPUs. Benchmarks consistently place the instance within average ranges, recording 34,691.95 on PassMark CPU, 12,045 on Geekbench multi-core, and 34.78 million Redis SET operations per second. With 4.8 GB of memory per core and consistent 3.1 GHz execution rates, this configuration is well matched for compute-heavy web application tiers, database operations, software build systems, and in-memory caches.
